To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) residual correlation is important in reactive transport parameter estimation, and (2) accounting for residual correlations can be done efficiently by integrating out the (covariance) parameters in a Bayesian approach

(1) accounting residual correlations between species is important for parameter estimation, (2) the multivariate approach provides the most accurate parameter estimates and is computationally more efficient than WLS and WLES, and (3).
the MV approach provides a more accurate parameter estimation than the WLS and the WLS(We) approach and that it is computationally less demanding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an efficient Bayesian approach to the inference of reactive transport parameters from multispecies data.
the formulation of the parameter estimation problem as a multivariate problem and the development of an efficient inference algorithm for this problem.
the development of an efficient approach for the inference of model parameters from multispecies data that accounts for residual correlation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, if residual correlation is not accounted for, parameter estimates will be biased and the predictive uncertainty will be underestimated, and if residual correlation is accounted for, the parameter estimates will be more accurate but the uncertainty will be overestimated.
the MV approach is the best method in the absence of model structural errors and that the WLS(We) is the best approach in the presence of structural errors.
the multivariate approach is superior to the other approaches in the sense that it provides a better balance between computational effort, parameter accuracy and predictive uncertainty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MV approach is the most efficient way of accounting for residual correlation in the presence of a limited number of measurements.
the WLS method is not recommended for parameter estimation in the case of multispecies data.
the WLS( we) method should be preferred when the residual correlation can be neglected, whereas the MV method should be preferred for high residual correlation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
residual correlation between species is a key aspect of multispecies reactive transport data and that a Bayesian multivariate inference approach can be used to efficiently account for this effect.
the MV method is able to account for residual correlation without the need for estimating the error parameters.

the Bayesian multivariate approach provides a framework for the estimation of model parameters from multispecies data that is more general than the common WLS and WSL(we) methods and that is able to handle residual correlations between species without the need for their explicit estimation.
